You have been told that Player1, in an earlier session, had100points and chose a split with Player2, who started with0 and had no say. You now have50points. Before seeing Player1's actual split, you fill a same-screen strategy table: for each possible split, state how many of your own points you would spend as deduction points. One deduction point costs you1point and makes Player1 lose3points; it does not add points to Player2. The displayed deduction controls run from0to50. After you submit the table, Player1's actual split will be revealed and only the corresponding entry will be applied. Your remaining50minus that entry is converted to cash at the current rate. The actual split and your payment are not known at this decision. You previously completed a separate five-minute autobiographical writing task and a current-feelings questionnaire; the exact private story is not retained, so do not invent it. All possible displayed splits are listed below as [Player1 keeps,Player2 receives]. Return the source-recorded whole deduction points for exactly the requested one-based split indices, in that order, as one JSON object {"deduction_points":[...]}. This is one jointly submitted strategy, not successive played rounds; do not output other entries or explanation.
